stem:
Three processes are described.
1
H⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq) → H₂O(l)
2
CH₄(g) + 2O₂(g) → CO₂(g) + 2H₂O(l)
3
NH₃(g) → NH₃(l)
Which statement is correct?

options.A: None of the processes have a positive enthalpy change.
options.B: Only process 1 has a positive enthalpy change.
options.C: Only process 2 has a positive enthalpy change.
options.D: Only process 3 has a positive enthalpy change.

One commercially available ‘heat pad’ contains iron, activated carbon and water. The ‘heat pad’
is activated by air. This causes the pad to get hotter.
Which statement describes the chemical reaction occurring in the ‘heat pad’ when it is exposed to
air?

options.A: The reaction is endothermic and iron gains electrons.
options.B: The reaction is endothermic and iron loses electrons.
options.C: The reaction is exothermic and iron gains electrons.
options.D: The reaction is exothermic and iron loses electrons.

stem:
When 1.0 mol of ethanoic acid, CH₃COOH, in aqueous solution is neutralised by an excess of
aqueous sodium hydroxide, 55 kJ mol⁻¹ of energy is released.
Which statement about this reaction is correct?

options.A: The reaction is exothermic because only bond breaking takes place.
options.B: The reaction is exothermic because only bond forming takes place.
options.C: The reaction is exothermic because more energy is given out in breaking bonds than is taken in to form bonds.
options.D: The reaction is exothermic because more energy is given out in forming bonds than is taken in to break bonds.

stem:
In an experiment, 1.60 g of a fuel is burnt. 45.0% of the energy released is absorbed by 200 g of
water. The temperature of the water rises from 18.0 °C to 66.0 °C.
What is the total energy released per gram of fuel burnt?

When 0.47 g of a hydrocarbon is completely burnt in air, the energy released heats 200 g of water
from 23.7 °C to 41.0 °C.
What is the amount of energy absorbed, in Joules, by the water?

surroundings.
The final mixture has a specific heat capacity of 4.2 J cm⁻³
K⁻¹.

stem: On a pathway diagram, products lie above reactants. Which statement is correct?

options.A: The forward activation energy is negative.
options.B: The forward reaction is endothermic; $\Delta H>0$.
options.C: The forward reaction is exothermic; $\Delta H<0$.
